conviction_note: The findings net to a small negative (-0.8). The CEO's mid-quarter open-market buy leans positive. Against it: the reaffirmed $882m guide that consensus sits on needs H2 growth to accelerate (+16.2% vs +14.3% in H1) while case volume slows and EOS must jump from $31m in H1 to $46m in H2. Hospital surgical volumes softened in Q3. abs_move 12 sits between the 10.2% event-implied move and the 12.9% median reaction, because this name moves 20-30% on the guidance line. p_up 47 because the evidence is mostly public arithmetic and inference, not an unpriced company number.

positioning_check: Short interest about 14.1M shares with 7.0 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 5.5 days on 2026-09-15 (FINRA via curvedtrading.com search snippet, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/atec/short-interest/; the page itself returned 403). findings.finding: Guidance arithmetic from the company's own releases. FY2026 revenue guide is about $882m, reaffirmed 2026-08-04, and consensus sits exactly on it at $882.06m. H1 revenue was $405.6m (+14.3% on $354.7m), so H2 needs $476.4m, +16.2% on H2'25's $410m. That is an acceleration while management guides H2 case volume down to high-teens from 20% and revenue per case down low single digits. It also needs EOS at about $46m in H2 (+7% y/y) against $31m in H1 (Q1 $14m, Q2 $17m, about -6% y/y), after EOS was cut twice already in 2026 ($85m in Feb, $77m in May). A trim of the revenue guide of about $5-10m at this print is the plausible route, even if EBITDA and FCF hold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance-line surprises moved this stock hard. 2026-05-05: -31.67% on a Q1 shortfall plus the EOS guide cut. 2026-01-12: -22.34%, when the initial $890m guide was given at JPM. 2026-08-04: -7.54% on a revenue reaffirm with an EBITDA raise. 2025's beat-and-raise prints: +16.29% and +30.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus FY revenue is pinned at $882.06m with a range of $881.8-882.6m, so the sell side models the guide being hit; a priced trim would show a consensus below $882m. Implied Q4 at Q3 consensus is +18% y/y, above every 2026 quarter's growth. Against that, the stock is 46% off its 52-week high, so some guide risk sits in the price, and the +22.5% 20-day run-up says the market has not been leaning on this.
findings.independence: Q1 release (EOS cut, $882m): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001350653/000119312526206530/atec-ex99_2.htm. Q4'25 release ($890m and EOS $85m): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1350653/000119312526067062/atec-ex99_1.htm. Q3'25 release (EOS $20m, surgical $177m): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1350653/000119312525258609/atec-ex99_1.htm. All are company documents, so this is one source family read as arithmetic. The H2 high-teens case volume comment comes from the Q2 call summary (https://quartr.com/events/alphatec-holdings-inc-atec-q2-2026_onKpLzDy). Net of the rest of the company: surgical (91% of revenue) beat consensus in Q2 by about 1% and could cover a few million of EOS shortfall.

findings.finding: Chairman and CEO Pat Miles bought 115,000 shares in the open market on 2026-09-10 at a weighted $8.81 (about $1.01m, Form 4 code P). That was ten weeks into Q3, with July and August trends in hand, and the day after the company's Wells Fargo conference fireside chat. It is his first open-market purchase in this record after years of reported sales. The stock is now $12.13.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior open-market CEO buy into a print is in the record. The quarterly reported-line reactions are in the baseline: the Q2 beat of about 1% got -7.5%, and the Q3'25 beat of about 7.6% with a raise got +16.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since 2026-09-10 and covered by Motley Fool on 2026-09-30, and the stock is +37% since. Much of it is likely in the price, which is why it is sized small. What is not priced is the inference that a CEO with mid-quarter data would not buy ahead of a guide cut. If the market fully believed that, the guide-trim risk in finding 1 would already be absent from the stock.
findings.independence: https://www.webull.com/news/15668339373261824 (Motley Fool, 2026-09-30) reports the same Form 4; it is one fact. Pointing the other way: General Counsel sold 8,168 shares on 2026-08-05 under a 10b5-1 plan for tax withholding (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-alphatec-nasdaq-atec-cut-to-hold-at-wall-street-zen-2026-10-11/), which is routine.

findings.finding: Hospital surgical volumes softened in Q3 2026. HCA same-facility inpatient surgeries fell 1.4% and outpatient surgeries 3.7% y/y (vs +1.4% and +1.1% in Q3'25), with a payer-mix hit from exchange coverage losses. Tenet's USPI same-facility surgical cases fell 1.5% (revenue per case +6.1%). Spine fusion is elective, so this is a mild headwind to the procedure base that ATEC's high-teens case growth assumes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of ATEC moving on hospital volume data. ATEC grows cases 20% on share gains, so the market has looked through the procedure market.
findings.why_not_priced: Hospital volume prints are read by hospital investors, not spine investors. ATEC rose 22.5% in the 20 days these prints arrived, which would not be the shape if the market had marked down elective spine volume. This is a proxy: neither ATEC nor a spine counterparty has confirmed transmission, and spine-specific series below point the other way.
findings.independence: Tenet Q3 2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000070318/000007031826000045/thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm. Contrary, broader spine series: Medtronic Cranial & Spinal low-double-digit organic (see the next finding).

findings.finding: Spine peers that reported after ATEC's 2026-08-04 print show market demand intact. Medtronic Cranial & Spinal Technologies grew about 13% (low-double-digit organic, enabling tech low-20s) in the May-July quarter, reported 2026-09-01; the extra fiscal week flattered it, and the Stealth AXiS launch is a direct competitor to ATEC's Valence enabling tech. Globus Q2 US spine grew +7.3%. J&J's Q3 2026 10-Q says Spine, Sports & Other grew on launches, offset by competition, consistent with continued share loss by the incumbent to share-takers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer read-throughs have not visibly driven ATEC's prints; ATEC's reactions turned on its own guide.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public and mostly priced. The residual is that the spine-specific series (MDT, GMED, J&J) are healthier than the hospital-wide surgical counts in the previous finding, and the market has had no ATEC data point since August. Mixed sign because MDT's enabling-tech launch competes directly.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-23 ATEC created a new EVP, Data Intelligence and Strategy role (Tommy Carls, ex-Medtronic/Proprio) that owns development and marketing for EOSedge and EOS Insight, with a 200,000-RSU grant (Form 4 dated 2026-10-05). EOS is the segment that missed twice in 2026, and the reorganisation suggests the company is still working on it heading into an H2 that needs a large EOS step-up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EOS shortfalls drove the 2026-05-05 -31.67% reaction, alongside a Q1 miss.
findings.why_not_priced: It was announced as a strategy hire and read as positive (Webull 'Is ATEC undervalued as Carls joins'), not as a signal on EOS run-rate. This is an inference with no number; it could equally be an investment in a working franchise, so it is sized very small.
findings.independence: Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1350653/000215578426000004/form4-10062026_121008.xml. It shares the EOS concern with finding 1 but rests on a different document.

baseline_tension: The skew is null, so the options say nothing about direction. The +22.5% 20-day run-up and the CEO buy lean bullish, while the guide arithmetic leans negative. The findings cut mildly against the run-up, and the about 10%-of-float short (7 days to cover) is a squeeze mechanism on any reaffirm, so p_up sits only slightly below 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, about 10% of float and 7 days to cover): guidance-arithmetic negative shrunk from -1.5 to -1.3.
Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; public since 2026-09-10 and the stock is +37% since): CEO buy shrunk from +1.0 to +0.8.
Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broader direct series): hospital surgical-volume proxy shrunk from -0.7 to -0.4, because spine-specific peer series are healthier.
Lesson 3 (own caveat must reach the number): the EOS-reorg inference shrunk from -0.3 to -0.2, since the hire could equally be an investment.
Lesson 9 (net of the rest): the guide finding states that surgical (91% of revenue) could cover part of an EOS gap; left at -1.3 after lesson 7.
